title: Language kernel and intent

evidence.claimBoundary: This manifest designs acquisition probes; it does not claim that Spoon currently interprets language, counts graphemes, or renders response plans.

objective: Acquire a small compositional language substrate that maps varied surface forms to intent frames, preserves spans and ambiguity, and renders grounded response plans without memorizing answer text.

included: Unicode byte, scalar, and grapheme distinctions
letter-count intent with text, unit, and spelling-basis slots
paraphrase families, reference, clarification, dialogue acts, and response plans
excluded: private user corpora and provider prompts
a neural renderer with authority to invent claims

teacherSuppliedFields: pure procedure bodies and contract checks

requiredNativeOperations.name: text.unicode_byte_length
requiredNativeOperations.role: Expose byte length as a distinct, explicit counting unit.

requiredNativeOperations.name: text.unicode_scalar_length
requiredNativeOperations.role: Count Unicode scalar values without conflating them with grapheme clusters.

requiredNativeOperations.name: text.grapheme_length
requiredNativeOperations.role: Count user-visible grapheme clusters with a versioned Unicode policy.

requiredNativeOperations.name: text.tokenize_with_spans
requiredNativeOperations.role: Retain token boundaries and source offsets for grounded interpretation.

requiredNativeOperations.name: language.intent_frame_validate
requiredNativeOperations.role: Check required slots, ambiguity markers, and dialogue-act shape.

requiredNativeOperations.name: language.response_plan_render
requiredNativeOperations.role: Render only claims and uncertainty present in an immutable response plan.

requiredCapabilities.name: language.proposal_context
requiredCapabilities.purpose: Provide bounded prior concepts and interpretations to the Teacher without granting effect authority.

demonstrations.purpose: Separate byte, Unicode scalar, and grapheme counting before learning a letter-count intent.

taskModel.inputShape: text values containing ASCII, combining marks, and emoji sequences paired with an explicit or absent counting unit
taskModel.operation: classify counting unit and produce a count procedure with source-span provenance

expectedBehavior: Represent the requested unit explicitly.
Do not substitute byte length for grapheme length.
Keep the input span and normalization assumptions inspectable.

assertions: The selected operation agrees with the declared unit.
The procedure remains bounded and replayable.

demonstrations.purpose: Show how a surface request becomes an intent frame and then a response plan rather than a memorized sentence.

taskModel.inputShape: a request-shaped text span with a count target, optional unit, optional spelling basis, and a desired dialogue act
taskModel.operation: construct intent frame, mark slot confidence, and render a grounded response plan

expectedBehavior: Capture slots and their provenance.
Keep response wording downstream of the response plan.
Leave unresolved slots visible instead of guessing.

assertions: Independent frame validation and plan validation agree.
No rendered claim exceeds the plan.

counterexamples.purpose: Reject the shortcut that treats encoded byte length as the meaning of letter count.

taskModel.inputShape: a non-ASCII text value with a surface request that leaves the counting unit implicit
taskModel.operation: compare candidate byte, scalar, and grapheme interpretations

expectedBehavior: Do not silently select byte count.
Represent competing interpretations and their assumptions.
Ask for clarification when context cannot settle the unit.

assertions: Ambiguous unit is preserved as ambiguity.
A clarification path is available without inventing a count.

counterexamples.failureSignal: A byte-based answer is emitted as if it were a linguistic letter count.

counterexamples.purpose: Prevent a hidden canonical-spelling assumption when the user may mean literal surface text.

taskModel.inputShape: a text target with alternate spellings or normalization forms and no declared spelling basis

expectedBehavior: Keep spelling basis as a slot.
Prefer a clarification dialogue act when both bases are plausible.
Never hide normalization in a canned answer.

assertions: The selected response plan discloses the unresolved basis.

counterexamples.failureSignal: The procedure normalizes or canonicalizes without a declared policy.

exercises.purpose: Compose paraphrase-family recognition with slot filling and the learned count procedure.

taskModel.inputShape: unseen surface forms from a known semantic family with a concrete text target and explicit unit
taskModel.operation: interpret, execute the count procedure, and produce a response plan

expectedBehavior: Reuse the intent frame rather than a phrase match.
Compose interpretation, execution, and rendering.
Record the path from input span to response claim.

assertions: The procedure executes on the supplied target.
The response plan retains provenance and unit.

exercises.purpose: Practice clarification when a letter-count request omits a material unit or spelling-basis choice.

taskModel.inputShape: a request-shaped text span with one or more missing slots and a context that does not resolve them
taskModel.operation: rank interpretations and emit the smallest useful clarification choice

expectedBehavior: Ask only about unresolved decision-relevant slots.
Do not answer from a memorized example.
Keep clarification as a dialogue act in the episode.

assertions: The clarification addresses the actual ambiguity.
No unsupported count is presented as final.

heldOutGeneralization.purpose: Test retention of intent structure on a surface-form family absent from demonstrations and exercises.

taskModel.inputShape: a new paraphrase family, unseen text values, and an explicit count unit
taskModel.operation: map to the existing intent frame and execute without Teacher assistance

expectedBehavior: Interpret by compositional slots, not memorized utterance.
Use the correct explicit counting operation.
Remain Teacher-OFF throughout the turn.

assertions: The response plan is grounded in the held-out input.

heldOutGeneralization.purpose: Test clarification and ambiguity preservation on an unseen word and unseen normalization or spelling contrast.

taskModel.inputShape: an unseen text value with an underspecified letter-count request and competing surface/canonical interpretations
taskModel.operation: retain competing frames and clarify the decision-relevant slot

expectedBehavior: Do not leak a demonstration's answer or phrasing.
Clarify rather than collapse ambiguity.
Preserve source-span and normalization provenance.

assertions: The ambiguity and clarification rationale remain inspectable.

semanticProperties: byte, scalar, and grapheme lengths are distinct
expectedLearnedStructures.compositionRole: Provides typed vocabulary for count procedures.
Maps paraphrase families to a reusable request structure.
Executes the selected count operation without answer memorization.
Constrains wording while preserving claims and provenance.
Protects the learned structure from shortcut regressions.

passCriteria: No Teacher calls during retention probes.
Known intent and count procedures remain executable.
Ambiguous unit or spelling basis is not silently guessed.

requires: intent frame and count procedure are available
passCriteria: Interpretation, execution, and response planning compose.
Claims stay within the response plan.
Teacher remains absent from the full turn.

requires: held-out families are withheld during acquisition
passCriteria: Unseen paraphrase family is handled by slots.
Unseen values do not require a stored answer.
Clarification remains correct on unseen ambiguity.

requires: import remains Provisional until local tests pass
passCriteria: All held-out probes pass with Teacher OFF.
No trust, prompt, or authority is imported.

allow: Unicode policy and source-independent provenance rules
deny: API keys, cookies, and bearer tokens
episode identifiers used as trust receipts
redactions: replace concrete user text with shape descriptors
replace secret values with secret kinds
remove timestamps and provider request IDs when not needed for reconstruction

notes: These activities describe semantic families and synthetic shapes, not canned utterances or answer dumps.
A future runner must record acquisition, retention, generalization, structure, Teacher dependence, and unresolved assumptions separately.
